results.summary: This project is a simplified Blackjack game implemented entirely in digital hardware. The core game logic, cards, rules and balance run as a finite-state machine, with a 16-bit LFSR used as a pseudo-random card generator. The player interacts using Hit, Stand, Double and Start push-buttons, and the internal state is visualized on a VGA blackjack table screen. All logic is fully synthesizable and fits into a single Tiny Tapeout tile.

results.summary: This tile integrates two independent analog designs in the SkyWater Sky130 130 nm PDK, sharing a single DC bias/control pin due to the 4-analog-pin Tiny Tapeout limit. One circuit is a current-controlled ring-oscillator VCO whose frequency appears on the digital output pin, and the other is a differential amplifier with input and output analog pins. Both circuits are permanently powered from VDD = 1.8 V and are tested through separate analog and digital pins. No external hardware is required beyond an Analog Discovery 3 or equivalent supply, function generator and oscilloscope or frequency counter.

results.summary: This design calculates the Fibonacci sequence up to 16 bits (max value 46,368 before overflow). A synchronous Fibonacci core advances whenever an external pulse is detected, and a Double Dabble binary-to-BCD converter produces five BCD nibbles in exactly 17 clock cycles. A ring-counter multiplexer enables one of the 5 digits at a time, synchronized with the main clock, and a combinational 7-segment decoder converts the current BCD nibble into the gfedcba pattern. The design includes a synchronizer and edge detector on the manual step input to ensure stable operation even with mechanical buttons.

results.summary: Katomata is a Tiny Tapeout demoscene entry: a 1D elementary cellular automata visualizer for VGA. It implements Stephen Wolfram's classification of Elementary Cellular Automata and continuously cycles through all 256 rules, drawing the time evolution of each rule directly on a 640x480 @ 60 Hz VGA frame. The design is driven by a 25.175 MHz pixel clock and requires a TinyVGA Pmod and a VGA monitor. There are no input pins to drive, as all ui_in and uio_in bits are unused.

results.summary_before: This project is a hardware implementation of a simple processor with a custom instruction set. It includes an ALU, register file, and control logic. The design is written in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It is notable for its minimalistic yet complete CPU architecture.
results.summary: The Lambda Clock is a full digital calendar and clock built for a 10-digit 7-segment multiplexed display architecture using three cascaded 74HC595 shift registers. It features a fully synchronous clock-enable domain that parses base 1 Hz and 1 kHz ticks to manipulate independent BCD limits, avoiding binary-to-BCD resource explosion, and it enforces leap-year restrictions automatically. An 8-state settings menu tracks and individually updates days, months, years and time, and a built-in alarm module is continuously checked against the current active BCD time registers. The design is written in Verilog and uses four push-buttons plus a buzzer and optional status LEDs.
